_what: Every artifact authored in BOSS's gitignored /.claude/ workspace, and whether it has crossed into the product a founder installs. THIS FILE IS TIER 2 — tracked here, absent from package.json `files:`, so it never reaches a founder's project.
_why: BOSS is self-hosted, so every agent and skill gets authored in the workspace first. Crossing is a deliberate act (/boss-learn routes it) and nothing caught what never got routed: 12 agents and 5 skills sat uncrossed and unexamined while shipped files pointed at four of them by name. `not-yet` is a legitimate verdict and always will be. `unexamined` is not — that is the only state this ledger exists to make impossible.

_verdicts.crossed: Ships under stages/*/template/ or library/. Verified to exist by check:boundary.
_verdicts.not-yet: Belongs to founders in principle; has not earned the port yet. Carries a reason, and the reason is re-read, not inherited.
_verdicts.internal: Examined, and the answer is no. Serves BOSS's own construction and would not survive contact with a founder's project.

_enforced_by: scripts/check-boundary.js — fails on an unexamined artifact, on a `crossed` verdict whose file does not exist, and on an `internal` or `not-yet` artifact that a shipped file names anyway.

artifacts.name: designer
artifacts.why: Designs BOSS's own interaction surface — when it speaks, what a skill feels like. A founder designing their product's surface is a different job, already held by ux-designer and ui-designer at L2. Would be rewritten, not ported.

artifacts.name: mentor-architect
artifacts.why: Ships at L1 — architecture decisions start mattering the moment there's a real build.

artifacts.name: mentor-business
artifacts.why: Ships at L2. Pricing and packaging are V1-era questions — asked earlier they invite a founder to monetize something nobody has used yet.

artifacts.name: mentor-fundraising
artifacts.why: Ships at L2, and defaults to "not yet" even there. Seated late on purpose: most projects reaching V1 still haven't earned the raise question.

artifacts.name: mentor-gtm
artifacts.why: Ships at L1 — distribution is an MVP-era question, not a V1 one.

artifacts.name: mentor-humane
artifacts.why: Deliberate, and already explained in public on site/team.html: an ethics mentor a founder can decline to open is weaker than a conscience they can't. The humane lens is cross-cutting — it lives in practices every mentor cites, not in one agent.

artifacts.name: mentor-pitch
artifacts.why: Ships at L2. The story is worth shaping once there is something to tell it about; before that it is rehearsal for a demo that doesn't exist.

artifacts.name: mentor-talent
artifacts.why: Ships at L2, defaulting to "not yet". First-hire questions arriving at MVP are almost always a delegation instinct firing early.

artifacts.name: mentor-venture
artifacts.why: The cornerstone. Ships at L0 and in library/, so every project has one mentor from the first minute.

artifacts.name: practice-refresh
artifacts.why: Refreshes BOSS's shelf, which is BOSS's job. But a founder's `/practice` PRAC records rot exactly the same way and nothing sweeps them. The founder version is a different, smaller skill — scoped to their records, not this one ported.

artifacts.name: recalibrate
artifacts.why: Since v0.135.0 BOSS pins no model names anywhere it ships (capability shapes, not names). There is nothing in a founder's project for this to recalibrate.

artifacts.name: regrade
artifacts.why: Re-grades BOSS's own conscience evals. A founder has no conscience evals.

artifacts.name: vet
artifacts.why: THE CLEAREST MISS. A founder faces "some thread says you must do X" constantly, and has nothing for it — while nine shipped practices were still pointing at this skill by name (fixed v0.178.0). 270 lines, so porting is real work, and the NO-biased rubric is tuned to BOSS's principles rather than a founder's. Port it scoped to the founder's own build, or don't; do not leave it unexamined.
